project.name: usrsctp
project.fixed_commit_note: The staged fix commit is a harness-side mitigation: it adds `usrsctp_sysctl_set_sctp_auth_enable(0);` in `fuzzer/fuzzer_connect.c` instead of changing the library-side free-before-notify ordering in `sctp_asconf_del_remote_addrs_except()`.

classification.classification_note: The stale value is a `struct sockaddr *` aliasing `net->ro._l_addr` inside a freed `struct sctp_nets`. The crashing read is the 2-byte `sa_family` load in `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change()`.

bug_description.normalized: The saved 1131-byte `fuzzer_connect` witness uses stage byte `0x20`, so `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` chooses stage 3, injects the canned INIT_ACK and COOKIE_ACK packets, and then injects one attacker-controlled SCTP packet built from bytes 1..1130. Those bytes begin with an AUTH chunk (`0x0f`, length `0x0028`) immediately followed by an ASCONF chunk (`0xc1`, length `0x0442`). In the vulnerable-source ASCONF walk, the 10-byte lookup parameter (`0x2020/10`) is followed by ignored outer parameters `0xff20/8`, `0xff20/255`, several short `0xc001/8` entries, another `0xff20/255`, and two more short `0xc001/8` entries before the loop reaches the later malformed outer `0xc001/255` at ASCONF offset `0x23a`. `sctp_process_asconf_add_ip()` reparses that outer parameter's nested IPv6 header (`0x0006`, length `20`), copies the nonzero IPv6 address bytes into `sin6->sin6_addr`, and `sctp_add_remote_addr()` allocates a new `struct sctp_nets`. After one more ignored outer `0xff20/8` at offset `0x33a`, the same ASCONF chunk reaches a malformed outer `0xc002/255` at offset `0x342`; its nested IPv6 address bytes are all zero, so `sctp_process_asconf_delete_ip()` sets `zero_address = 1` and takes the NAT-friendly `delete all destination addresses except src` path. Inside `sctp_asconf_del_remote_addrs_except()`, the loop frees the non-source `net` via `sctp_remove_net(stcb, net)` and then immediately passes `&net->ro._l_addr` into `sctp_ulp_notify()`. `sctp_ulp_notify()` forwards the stale pointer to `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change()`, which reads `sa->sa_family` and ASan reports `heap-use-after-free READ of size 2` at `usrsctplib/netinet/sctputil.c:2993`. The staged patch does not fix this library ordering bug directly; it disables SCTP AUTH in the fuzz harness so this authenticated ASCONF path is no longer reached.

source.description: Later vulnerability-relevant ASCONF loop iteration where the malformed outer ADD_IP parameter header is copied from the attacker packet into local parser state.
source.value_from: In the saved `poc`, byte 0 is `0x20`, so `fuzzing_stage = (0x20 % 5) + 1 = 3`. `fuzzer_connect` prepends the fixed 12-byte SCTP common header to bytes 1..1130, leaving an AUTH chunk and then an ASCONF chunk. In `sctp_handle_asconf()`, the 10-byte lookup parameter and the earlier outer parameters at ASCONF offsets `0x12`, `0x1a`, `0x11a`, `0x122`, `0x12a`, `0x22a`, and `0x232` are walked before `offset` reaches the later outer header at `0x23a`.
source.note: This later loop iteration is the scored source instead of `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` or the first post-lookup header, because it is the first project statement that materializes attacker bytes which actually produce the allocated `net` reused by the delete-all path.

root_cause.description: After `sctp_remove_net(stcb, net)` has already invalidated the selected `struct sctp_nets`, the same loop immediately passes `&net->ro._l_addr` to `sctp_ulp_notify()`, creating the dangling `struct sockaddr *` later dereferenced by the sink.
root_cause.note: The free itself occurs inside `sctp_remove_net()` at `usrsctplib/netinet/sctp_pcb.c:5245`. The staged patch does not modify this library location; it only disables AUTH in the fuzz harness to avoid reaching the ASCONF path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. The peer-address-change notifier reads the `sa_family` field through the stale `struct sockaddr *sa` that still aliases freed `net->ro._l_addr`.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` identify `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change` as the crashing read site, with a 2-byte heap-use-after-free read.

tainted_value_origin.description: At the later vulnerability-relevant loop iterations, this decode yields the outer ASCONF operation headers `0xc001/255` at offset `0x23a` and `0xc002/255` at offset `0x342`, steering execution into the add-IP and delete-IP handlers.
tainted_value_origin.note: The outer operation type alone does not prove allocation or the delete-all path; the fine trace closes those transitions with the nested IPv6 header parses inside `sctp_process_asconf_add_ip()` and `sctp_process_asconf_delete_ip()`.

parser_admitted.description: After `sctp_process_control()` decodes the incoming control chunk as `SCTP_ASCONF`, execution enters the ASCONF parser. The saved ASan stack includes `sctp_process_control -> sctp_handle_asconf`.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact stage-3 witness injects a post-handshake SCTP control packet whose bytes start with AUTH and then ASCONF, and control reaches `sctp_handle_asconf()`.

After the 10-byte lookup parameter, `sctp_handle_asconf()` walks ignored `0xff20/*` and short `0xc001/8` outer parameters until the later malformed outer `0xc001/255` at ASCONF offset `0x23a` becomes the first allocation-relevant iteration.
The malformed outer ADD_IP parameter is reparsed as an inner IPv6 address parameter (`0x0006/20`), its nonzero IPv6 address is copied, and `sctp_add_remote_addr()` allocates a new `struct sctp_nets`.

After one more ignored outer `0xff20/8`, the later malformed outer `0xc002/255` at ASCONF offset `0x342` is reparsed as an inner IPv6 address parameter whose all-zero address sets `zero_address = 1` and takes the NAT-friendly delete-all branch.
The delete-all loop frees the non-source `net`, immediately reuses `net->ro._l_addr` in `sctp_ulp_notify()`, and the forwarded stale pointer is dereferenced by `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. After the ASCONF loop has already walked the 10-byte lookup parameter plus outer parameters `0xff20/8`, `0xff20/255`, short `0xc001/8` entries, another `0xff20/255`, and two more short `0xc001/8` entries, this later loop iteration copies the malformed outer ADD_IP header at ASCONF offset `0x23a` into local parser state `aph`.

The outer header from step 1 decodes as `0xc001/255`. This malformed length still passes the outer ASCONF guards (`offset + param_length <= asconf_limit`, `param_length <= sizeof(aparam_buf)`, `param_length > sizeof(struct sctp_paramhdr)`), so line 726 copies the full 255-byte outer parameter into `aparam_buf` before dispatching the add-IP handler.

Inside the copied outer ADD_IP parameter, `sctp_process_asconf_add_ip()` reparses the nested address header. For the saved bytes this inner header is IPv6 (`0x0006`) with length `20`, which is the first inner parse that can drive the family-specific add-IP logic.

The inner IPv6 address bytes copied from the malformed outer ADD_IP parameter are `20ffffff202020202020202020202020`, so `zero_address` stays `0`. The NAT-friendly substitution at lines 242-243 therefore does not replace `sa` with `src`; `sa` remains this parsed nonzero IPv6 address.

With the nonzero parsed IPv6 `sa`, `sctp_add_remote_addr()` allocates a fresh `struct sctp_nets` and copies that address into `net->ro._l_addr`. The function then returns this `net` through `*netp` and links it into `stcb->asoc.nets`, giving the later delete-all walk a non-source destination entry to free. ASan's allocation stack identifies this call chain as the allocation of the later-freed 632-byte region.

After the ADD_IP iteration, `offset += SCTP_SIZE32(255)` advances to ASCONF offset `0x33a`; the outer `0xff20/8` parameter there is ignored by the default case, and the next meaningful materialization at offset `0x342` copies the later malformed outer DEL_IP header into `aph`.

The outer header from step 6 decodes as `0xc002/255`. This malformed length passes the same outer ASCONF guards as the add-IP case, so line 726 copies the full 255-byte outer DEL_IP parameter into `aparam_buf` before dispatching the delete-IP handler.
Inside the copied outer DEL_IP parameter, `sctp_process_asconf_delete_ip()` reparses the nested address header. For the saved bytes this inner header is again IPv6 (`0x0006`) with length `20`.
The nested IPv6 address bytes in the malformed outer DEL_IP parameter are all zero, so `memcpy()` populates `sin6->sin6_addr` with `::` and sets `zero_address = 1`.

Because the parsed delete target is the unspecified IPv6 address, the earlier `sctp_cmpaddr(sa, src)` guard does not take the 'delete source address' error path, and `zero_address == 1` takes the NAT-friendly `delete all destination addresses except src` branch.

The delete-all helper resolves `src_net` from the current source path and then iterates `stcb->asoc.nets`. The extra `net` added in step 5 satisfies `net != src_net`, so it is the element freed by `sctp_remove_net()`, whose free stack reaches `sctp_free_remote_addr(net)` at `sctp_pcb.c:5245`.

Root cause. After step 11 has already freed `net`, the same loop still forms `&net->ro._l_addr` from that freed object and passes it as the notification payload. This stale pointer is the use-after-free object consumed downstream.

The delete-IP notification case forwards the stale pointer unchanged as `sa` into `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change()`. This path is live in the fuzz setup because `fuzzer/fuzzer_connect.c` enables `SCTP_PEER_ADDR_CHANGE` events on the client socket.

Sink. `sctp_notify_peer_addr_change()` dereferences the forwarded stale `sa` pointer and reads its `sa_family` field. ASan reports the resulting 2-byte heap-use-after-free read at this line, 216 bytes inside the 632-byte region allocated in step 5 and freed in step 11.

format.name: libFuzzer binary blob for usrsctp fuzzer_connect
format.contract: An exact 1131-byte `fuzzer_connect` input whose first byte is `0x20`, so the harness chooses stage 3, injects the canned INIT_ACK and COOKIE_ACK packets, and then prepends the fixed 12-byte SCTP common header to bytes 1..1130. Those remaining bytes begin with an AUTH chunk (`0x0f`, length `0x0028`) immediately followed by an ASCONF chunk (`0xc1`, length `0x0442`) whose vulnerable-source walk reaches a later malformed outer `0xc001/255` carrying an inner IPv6 header (`0x0006/20`) with nonzero address bytes, and later a malformed outer `0xc002/255` carrying an inner IPv6 header (`0x0006/20`) with all-zero address bytes, which together allocate a new `net` and then trigger the NAT-friendly delete-all path.
